ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are five triangles arranged around the same center point, and each triangle has one vertex at the center point. At the other two outer vertices of each triangle, a gray angle is marked, so a total of 5×2=10 angles are marked. At the center point, several straight lines intersect to form the central vertex angles of these triangles. Reasoning: Regard the figure as five triangles sharing a center point. Let the angles of these five triangles at the center point be c1,c2,c3,c4,c5 respectively. Since these central angles are alternating angles formed by five straight lines passing through the center point, their sum is 180°. For each triangle, the two outer marked angles plus the corresponding central angle equal 180°. Therefore the sum of all the outer marked angles of the five triangles is 5×180°−(c1+c2+c3+c4+c5)=900°−180°=720°.

raw_record.question_text: What is the sum of the 10 angles marked in the picture?

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as five triangles sharing a common central point. The 10 shaded angles are the two outer angles of these five triangles. At the center, observe that the triangle vertex angles are alternating angles formed by five straight lines passing through the common point, so these five central angles sum to 180°. For each triangle, the two shaded angles plus its central angle sum to 180°. Therefore the total of all 10 shaded angles is 5·180° − 180° = 720°.
